comments.content: - `src/misc/lv_text.c:653` — The NULL guard applies only to the UTF-8 decoder. With `LV_TXT_ENC == LV_TXT_ENC_ASCII`, calling `lv_text_encoded_letter_next_2(NULL, &letter, &letter_next, &ofs)` dispatches to `lv_text_iso8859_1_next`, which dereferences `txt` and crashes instead of returning zeroed letters with an unchanged offset.

**DEFECT 1: `src/misc/lv_text.c:653` — Uninitialized `result` returned on NULL/empty input**

The added early-return `if(txt == NULL || txt[*i] == '\0') return result;` returns `result` before it is ever assigned. In the original code, `result` is only assigned inside the `if(LV_IS_ASCII(...))` branch and subsequent UTF-8 branches (not shown in diff). Calling `lv_text_utf8_next(NULL, ...)` or `lv_text_utf8_next("", ...)` now returns an indeterminate `uint32_t` value instead of a defined sentinel (e.g., 0).

**Failure scenario:** `lv_text_utf8_next(NULL, &idx)` → returns garbage (stack contents) → caller treats garbage as a valid code point → buffer overrun or logic corruption downstream.
